expectations.text: All 5 Jonah Rhythm steps are present: Emma catalyzes, Emma exits, James struggles, James discovers, Emma returns
expectations.evidence: Emma catalyzes: shows the TypeError, asks James to read the traceback, gives him the print(type(...)) technique (lines 5-16). Emma exits: 'She picked up her coffee mug. "I need to hop on a standup call. Fifteen minutes."' (line 15-16). James struggles: types the print statement, identifies 'price' is a string, traces it to CSV reader (lines 21-28). James discovers: creates the parse_number helper function to centralize conversion, recognizing the pattern (lines 36-41). Emma returns: 'The door opened. Emma set her coffee down' (line 45), validates and names the pattern (lines 45-61). All five steps are clearly present and in the correct order.

expectations.text: Emma's exit has a natural reason
expectations.evidence: 'I need to hop on a standup call. Fifteen minutes.' (line 15). A standup call is a routine engineering meeting, natural and specific.

James types the diagnostic print statement (line 21), stares at the CSV origin of the string (line 25-26), thinks about the category of problem (lines 27-28), adds the float conversion (line 29), then realizes his fix is brittle: 'something nagged him' (line 35), 'playing whack-a-mole' (line 35). The struggle is multi-phase: diagnosis, then first fix, then recognition that the first fix is insufficient.

expectations.text: James makes a genuine partial discovery on his own
expectations.evidence: James goes beyond the simple float() fix to create a parse_number helper function (lines 36-39), recognizing the pattern: 'conversion logic belongs in one place, not scattered across every line that touches the data' (line 41). This is a genuine architectural insight, not just bug-fixing. The discovery is partial because he hasn't handled edge cases (the 'N/A' input Emma will raise).

expectations.text: Emma's return validates James's discovery AND fills the remaining gap
expectations.evidence: Validates: 'That's actually a pattern worth naming. The Single Conversion Point' (line 49). She explicitly names and elevates his discovery. Fills gap: 'What happens if someone passes it the string "N/A"?' (line 57). This identifies the edge case his helper function doesn't handle, pointing toward error handling as the next layer. She also adds fallibility: 'I still catch myself doing the inline fix when I'm tired' (line 53).
